prompt: Why does the lesson call Content Security Policy a second line of defence?

choices.why: It has nothing to do with sign-in.

choices.why: Right. It does not replace escaping.

choices.text: It runs on a second server
choices.why: It is a header the browser enforces.

choices.text: It only applies to the second page a patient visits
choices.why: It applies to every page that carries it.

prompt: How does the fix replace the `onclick` attribute?

choices.text: With an onclick in the script tag
An id on the button, and addEventListener in the file
choices.why: Right. Code in a file, not code in an attribute.

prompt: A page needs the patient's id in its script. Which way keeps the policy strict?

choices.text: A fixed nonce written once in the code
choices.why: A fixed nonce is a password written in the page.

choices.text: A data- attribute, read by the script file
Put the id in the page title
choices.why: Still needs code to read it, and leaks it to history.

prompt: Why is adding a host to `script-src` a review, not a routine change?

choices.text: Browsers allow only one host per policy

prompt: Why keep what `/csp-report` logs short?

choices.why: Right. Log a little, with %r, and rate-limit it.
